rationale: The literature on TUBA4A-associated spastic ataxia (SPAX11; OMIM #621226) demonstrates a core phenotype defined by spasticity and progressive cerebellar ataxia without early-stage dementia, visual degeneration (retinopathy/optic atrophy characteristic of SCA7), or isolated lower motor neuron degeneration. Studies delineating the neurodegenerative and neuromuscular spectrum of TUBA4A variants confirm that SPAX11 presents with upper motor neuron signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, extensor plantar responses) and cerebellar dysfunction, distinct from the frontotemporal dementia/amyotrophic lateral sclerosis spectrum (FTDALS9) also linked to TUBA4A. Animal models engineered with SPAX11-associated variants exhibit ataxia, spasticity, and Purkinje cell loss without motor neuron disease pathology, supporting the exclusion of isolated lower motor neuron denervation from the SPAX11 definition.

evidence.text: Screening of 448 ataxia probands and 100KGP data identified 12 patients with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia bearing TUBA4A missense variants. The presentation is designated hereditary spastic ataxia with variable age of onset, distinguishing it from FTD/ALS presentations associated with other TUBA4A mutations.

source.title: De novo and inherited monoallelic variants in TUBA4A cause ataxia and spasticity
source.quote: Taken together, we report 12 patients presenting with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia and harbouring a predicted pathogenic TUBA4A missense mutation, including five confirmed de novo cases and a mutation previously reported in a large family presenting with spastic ataxia... Our data confirm the identification of a hereditary spastic ataxia disease gene with variable age of onset, expanding the clinical spectrum of TUBA4A associated phenotypes.

evidence.text: Characterization of two families (one with 11 affected individuals and another single patient) with the TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys mutation established spastic ataxia as a discrete clinical entity different from prior ALS/FTD phenotypes.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: In the present study, we report two families, one with 11 affected individuals and the other with a single patient, carrying a novel, likely pathogenic, variant (p. Glu415Lys) in the TUBA4A gene (NM_006000). The phenotype, not previously described, is that of spastic ataxia. Our findings widen the phenotypic and genetic manifestations of TUBA4A variants and add a new type of spastic ataxia to be taken into consideration in the differential diagnosis.

evidence.text: A mouse model of dominant spastic ataxia caused by Tuba4a p.Gln176Pro recapitulates hallmark Purkinje neuron degeneration and ataxia without motor neuron degeneration or phenotypes consistent with motor neuron disease, separating SPAX11 pathology from pure motor neuron disorders.

source.title: A mouse model of autosomal dominant spastic ataxia and myopathy caused by a mutation in Tuba4a
source.quote: Dominant TUBA4A mutations in humans are associated with spastic ataxia type 11 (SPAX11), congenital myopathy type 26 (CMYO26), and frontotemporal dementia/amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 9 (FTDALS9). Our mice exhibit hallmark features of SPAX11 and CMYO26, but do not show motor neuron degeneration.

numbers.metric: age of overt ataxia onset in mice (days)

evidence.text: Comprehensive analysis of TUBA4A disease manifestations delineates myo-tubulinopathies and multisystem proteinopathies from pure neurodegenerative phenotypes, noting that pure myopathy presentations lack CNS involvement, while spastic ataxia remains a distinct central syndrome.

source.title: Missense variants in TUBA4A cause myo-tubulinopathies
source.quote: While previous studies have linked de novo or dominantly inherited TUBA4A missense variants to neurodegenerative phenotypes, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, frontotemporal dementia, spastic ataxia, and recently, an isolated congenital myopathy, the full phenotypic and genotypic spectrum of TUBA4A-related disorders remains incompletely characterised... Remarkably, individuals in 17 families presented with a myopathy without any CNS involvement or history of such disease.

new_directions.question_text: Does subclinical peripheral neuropathy or lower motor neuron loss occur late in SPAX11 progression as seen in other complex spastic ataxias?
new_directions.rationale: While early lower motor neuron denervation argues against SPAX11 and toward ALS, longitudinal electrophysiological studies in aged SPAX11 cohorts are needed to test whether late secondary axonal neuropathy develops.

new_directions.question_text: What structural domain specificity explains why certain TUBA4A variants (e.g., p.Glu415Lys) cause spastic ataxia whereas others cause FTDALS or isolated congenital myopathy?
new_directions.rationale: Mapping microtubule-binding interfaces and lattice destabilization rates across variant classes could identify precise biochemical predictors of spastic ataxia versus motor neuron or muscle degeneration.
